ai.title: SDK 0.10.7 adds applypatch tool and simplifies writefile
ai.summary: SDK 0.10.7 introduces `apply_patch` for Codex-compatible code editing and refactors `write_file` into a deterministic create/replace tool. `write_file` no longer supports edit snippet comments like `// ... rest of the function ...`, requiring `str_replace` or `apply_patch` for partial updates. This change applies to the `@codebuff/sdk` package.

eli5.text: If you write code that uses the assistant, you now have a new way to make small edits to existing files, similar to how Codex-based assistants edit code. The old method of replacing whole files still works the same, but it no longer guesses at keeping parts of the previous file when you leave placeholder comments like "//... rest of the function..." instead requiring you to overwrite the entire file. This is live today for users of the SDK package, and if you relied on those placeholder comments, you will need to switch to the new editing tool or the replacement method to make partial updates.

ai.title: Codebuff SDK version bump to 0.10.7
ai.summary: The @codebuff/sdk package is version-bumped from 0.10.6 to 0.10.7, bundling prior SDK changes. This release introduces the Codex-compatible apply_patch tool for file operations and refactors write_file into a deterministic create/replace tool, removing edit snippet support from the agent types, editor prompts, and common/src/tools/params/tool/write-file.ts. Models must now output full file contents for write_file invocations, as lazy edits using placeholder comments like // ... existing code ... are no longer parsed by the placeholder logic deleted from common/src/util/string.ts and packages/agent-runtime/src/fast-rewrite.ts.
ai.evidence: Commit b226f465 modifies sdk/package.json, bumping the version field for @codebuff/sdk from 0.10.6 to 0.10.7.

eli5.text: This release adds a new way to edit files using familiar diff-style changes, plus clearer guidance on subscription plans and usage limits. It also makes code generation more reliable by requiring the full file content instead of partial snippets, and introduces new agent types for code review and deep reasoning. The web pricing page now shows exactly how many credits you get per dollar, with helpful explanations of what each mode and limit covers, and an Account section in your profile lets you see your email and verification status. Upgrading gives you more transparent billing, safer auto top-ups that ask before charging you, and an easier path to start building projects for free directly from AI-generated plans.
